video_title: Draymond Green Reacts to Jaylen Brown Trade + Ice Cube Joins To Talk LeBron, Friday & Big 3

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Jaylen Brown trade to the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: You hardly see players, especially great young players, sent away to inter-division rivalry teams.
quotes.quote: The biggest move thus far is the Jaylen Brown trade. You hardly see players, especially great young players, sent away to inter-division rivalry teams. I remember one year Al Horford leaving the Celtics and going to the Philadelphia 76ers and everybody was like, 'What the hell, why would he do that?' Well, now you have the Boston Celtics trading one of their star players, homegrown, a guy who they drafted, a guy who has grown up in this league as a Boston Celtic, became a champion as a Boston Celtic, a Finals MVP as a Boston Celtic, Jaylen Brown, traded to the Philadelphia 76ers for Paul George, two first-round picks, a pick swap, and two second-round picks.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green argues the Jaylen Brown trade is not an even swap
quotes.excerpt: No disrespect to Paul George, but this isn't an even swap.
quotes.quote: No disrespect to Paul George, but this isn't an even swap. I have a lot of love for PG, but like myself, PG is 36 years old. I'm going into year 15, I think PG is going into year 17. And Jaylen Brown, not even 30 years old, he's 29 years old, and he's going into year 11. And by the way, he won Finals MVP two years ago. I think he just made all-NBA second team this year, and was arguably, possibly could have been a first-team performer, but the votes are what they are. So it's not an even swap when you're talking player for player.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Lakers acquiring Walker Kessler
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers make a splash acquiring Walker Kessler from the Jazz for an unprotected first-round pick.
quotes.quote: The Lakers make a splash acquiring Walker Kessler from the Jazz for an unprotected first-round pick in 2031 and 2033, first-round pick swaps in 28 and 30. They also gave him a four-year $130 million extension. The Lakers now have no tradeable first-round picks over the next seven years. The Lakers also have been searching for a center for years, and I think they finally feel like they've got their guy. I hope they got their guy because this really puts handcuffs on improving this roster for years to come. And this got to be a guy who ultimately makes them a championship-caliber team because between his contract and Luka's contract, and Luka's contract is only going to go up, Austin Reaves' new contract, they are really in a tight spot of what they can do to improve this team.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Clippers trading Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers trade Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Grady Dick, two first-round picks.
quotes.quote: The Clippers trade Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Grady Dick, two first-round picks, one pick swap, and two second-round picks. And Kawhi is back where he won a championship, where he delivered for an entire country, for an entire organization that had never been champions before. The Clippers are pretty much seemingly in a full rebuild at this point, getting under the tax and all of those different things. But the Raptors, I bet you the Raptors feel like they have a chance, mixing Kawhi with Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett. Wouldn't be surprised if you see RJ Barrett on the move at some point, just with how it's starting to shape up with guys who need the basketball in their hands and different things. But we shall see. As far as you're going to need some shooting, so we'll see if RJ Barrett is still there by the time this season kicks off.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Ice Cube on the Lakers' offseason moves
quotes.excerpt: First, I want to thank LeBron for coming to the Lakers and winning a championship.
quotes.quote: First, I want to thank LeBron for coming to the Lakers and winning a championship. People may have their comments about it, but everybody wanted it and and he brought it to LA. So, so um you got to salute him for that. He didn't have to come, could have went to a different team. Um got his son in the league, you know. I don't have no problems with fathers, you know, doing what they need to do to help their kids excel. Um and so, you know, first of all, you know, thanks for for balling out in LA.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Clippers' new arena and identity
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers got a new arena all that stuff, right in Inglewood.
quotes.quote: Kawhi just left the Clippers. And the Clippers got a new arena all that stuff, right in Inglewood. But we're in LA. I know you've said before, you've always clowned the idea of LA ever belonging to anyone outside of the purple and gold. What can the Clippers do as a franchise? Does that win championships? Would it ever matter to the city of LA? What can they do to kind of close that gap in who the Los Angeles Lakers are, who the Los Angeles Clippers are? Is that even possible?

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Ice Cube on the difficulty of the Clippers challenging the Lakers' legacy
quotes.excerpt: There's so much history to uproot the Lakers, you know, maybe have a dynasty and win three or four in a row.
quotes.quote: There's so much history to uproot the Lakers, you know, maybe have a dynasty and win three or four in a row, you know, which you got to win one in a row before you can even do that. So it it um it's a hard mountain to climb. It it always have been. Um you know, it's it's just always been a like I always wondered why LA. I mean economically I see. It's a major city that has a lot of ways to to get revenue from this city. Um but you know, it's like trying to take a new team to Boston and and trying to uproot what they've built. It just it's just not not I don't see it happening in my lifetime, so I'm not planning on living a long time.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Lakers' identity and arena
quotes.excerpt: I thought there was a chance, you know, that Steve Ballmer would take their the team and move it to Seattle.
quotes.quote: I thought there was a chance, you know, that Steve Ballmer would take their the team and move it to Seattle, right? Because I just felt like the history, to your point, like that they would never quite be able to jump over. And even when you go into into a dome now, it's great, it's huge, it's they did an incredible job with it. But it feels like the Lakers should be there. Like it feels like the presence of the Clippers don't quite fit that major of a thing in this city. At least that's what I feel.

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Ice Cube on the Clippers' history and fan base
quotes.excerpt: Look, they've done it before in some ways, you know, Lob City, that era with, you know, CP3 and and Blake.
quotes.quote: Look, they've done it before in some ways, you know, Lob City, that era with, you know, CP3 and and Blake and all, you know, that era was almost there. You know, they almost had the fever. But but even if they had won a championship, it's not going to take anything away from the Lakers, you know. They would have to win so many. Um and maybe they planning on doing it. Um but it's not impossible because they do have fans. There are, you know, a, you know, the Clipper fans are thick, you know, but they just can't, you know, compete, you know, with the with the love that the Lakers have in the city of Los Angeles.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on Michael Beasley's impact on the Big 3
quotes.excerpt: One name that's really become synonymous with the Big 3, in my opinion, I think, from a player standpoint, I just, and watching as a fan, would say it's the face, when it comes to a player, is Michael Beasley.
quotes.quote: One name that's really become synonymous with the Big 3, in my opinion, I think, from a player standpoint, I just, and watching as a fan, would say it's the face, when it comes to a player, is Michael Beasley, you know, who, as talented as a guy that I've ever had to guard, um, but also as outspoken as anyone kind of not in the NBA but in the basketball world. You know, what has it been like having a Michael Beasley in the league, kind of driving things for? He he I think he automatically just by the way he approaches it, kind of raised the intensity level of the games that he's a part of, uh, you know, the games you're looking forward to. What's it been like having a Mike Beasley a part of this league?

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Ice Cube on Michael Beasley's role in the Big 3
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, it's been great. He's, you know, box office as far as people want to see him play.
quotes.quote: Yeah, it's been great. He's, you know, box office as far as people want to see him play. Um, you know, he's still a great player, um, in this format, five-on-five, you know, one-on-one, whatever, you know, whatever situation you put him in with the basketball in his hand, he's great. He's our two-time MVP, uh, you know, a champion in the Big 3. Um, so, you know, we like personality. We don't shy away from people being themselves. Just don't want them to take it overboard. Um, that's all, and you know, he he's great. He know where the line is and he walks he walks the line most of the time. Uh, sometimes it goes over it a little bit and that's cool. We we deal with that.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Big 3's growth and NBA relationship
quotes.excerpt: You guys are aiming to become the first publicly traded, um, professional sports league in America.
quotes.quote: You guys are aiming to become the first publicly traded, um, professional sports league in America. Talk to me about that process, um, and as much as you can, right? Like I understand the, you know, the SEC and all of that stuff. Like, you know, when you guys are targeting becoming a publicly traded league, if you can share that. Uh, but just also kind of the, the the thought process behind, uh, wanting to take the league public as opposed to it being a privately funded league like it's been the, uh, first nine years of it.

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Big3 league growth and increasing television ratings
quotes.excerpt: we're not only retaining our audience, but we're building an audience of fans who love the Big 3
quotes.quote: I think we're at an inflection point in the league. We've calibrated the game, we have a loyal fan base, our ratings on CBS was up 23% from last year, week two. So, we're not only retaining our audience, but we're building an audience of fans who love the Big 3, the style of play.

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Allowing fans to invest in the Big3 league ownership
quotes.excerpt: why not let them take this ride to the top with us
quotes.quote: When you look down the road to expand and keep going, you have to start talking to the usual people, the billionaires with all the money. The same guys who own every other league are going to own this one. I'm not hating on that, but I'm saying why not give regular fans a shot at it. They've been with us nine years. We plan to be here 99 more or more. So, why not let them take this ride to the top with us, and not only just watch or get merchandise or bet on the game or come to the game, but now you're invested in the league for real. You're invested in the growth of the league and when you buy that merch, you know you growing your own investment. It just makes sense. I'm surprised that we're the first professional league to do this.

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA considering adopting Big3 one-shot free throw rule
quotes.excerpt: The NBA is thinking about taking one of our rules, one shot free throws.
quotes.quote: We love changing the game. The NBA is thinking about taking one of our rules, one shot free throws. I don't know if it works for full court, but it works for us and we'll see how it works full court.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Big 3's relationship with the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I've been I've been suspended from the NBA, um, as many times as anyone or ejected and fined.
quotes.quote: I've been I've been suspended from the NBA, um, as many times as anyone or ejected and fined and all the other stuff. And I know kind of how our process is in the NBA where, you know, you get a call from like, um, NBA security. You talk to them, they ask you all these dumbass questions, um, they talk to you like you dumb as hell and I hate it. One time I turned down doing an interview, like they want to find you for that. Um, but I know how that process go. What's the process like when you have a situation like that? Like is it you on the phone with Michael Beasley, is it like some some other people are on your staff? Like how how much are these guys interacting with you, the founder of the league as opposed to like, I'm on the phone with NBA, this NBA security guy who's asking me like these dumbass questions and it's like, bro, you you have the video right there, like why are you asking me this? Like what's that process like for you?

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Ice Cube on the Big 3's disciplinary process
quotes.excerpt: Clyde Drexler is the commissioner of the league, so he's definitely talking to the players.
quotes.quote: I mean they usually have my number, so we can always talk face-to-face or text. Um, Clyde Drexler is the commissioner of the league, so he's definitely talking to the players. Uh, you know, we huddle up with Clyde Drexler and, you know, he makes his decision. We respect him as the commissioner. Um, so, you know, what he decides, we back him on and roll with as a league and then try to explain to the players why this happened. It hasn't happened that often, um, in these nine years, because we're not, you know, we're not into fining and suspending people and, you know, all that, you know, it's like, if it goes too far, we do have to do what we need to do to keep the integrity of the league. We got CBS, you know, kind of, um, really wanting us to monitor things and not let them get out of hand, you know, we on a major network. And so, uh, we all got to abide by certain rules. And so, Clyde Drexler say here's what he think it should be, uh, we discuss it and he he usually makes the call. And then I usually get a text. You know, Cube, man, this is fucked up, man. Cube, man, I didn't do nothing, man. Why? Why? Why? Why? And I'm like, uh, here's the explanation, bruh. And uh, we love you, uh, but let's just play basketball.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Big 3's disciplinary process

quotes.quote: Adam is definitely got some of those texts from me, so I get it. He's definitely got some of those. Yeah, you don't see me at the podium, I retired. But uh but but but you know, I'm I'm you know, I'm I'm really looking for people who use basketball to help people, uh not necessarily on the court, but off the court.

So, now it's the Luka era, and we'll see, you know, um, some of these moves have have raised eyebrows, you know, they calling it the snow time Lakers and, you know, we'll see, we'll see, um, you know, we'll see if they, if they can, uh, I don't mind that name, earn it, you know. I mean Showtime is a, uh, is a big name to, uh, to live up to. So, we'll see what they do, you know, um, I'm a wait and see kind of guy, so I'm not going to count them out. But you know, you going to be on the court with them, what you think?

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Ice Cube on the Big 3's mission and player selection
quotes.excerpt: We give it to people who use their, um, whatever they have off the court.
quotes.quote: We give it to people who use their, um, whatever they have off the court, um, you know, whatever they are doing great off the court to help people through the game of basketball, that's what we, you know, we want to award those people. You know, maybe not players that score, you know, 100 points, 81 points, whatever, but we want to honor people that's on the sideline, the coaches, the mentors, the people who, um, you know, have a connection to basketball and use that to, you know, help stooms or help, uh, you know, underprivileged people or underprivileged kids, you know, just to, you know, have a have a a better life and using basketball to better people's lives. And that's what I've done, and I can't I don't play. I play, but I, you know, I'm retired. But uh but but but you know, I'm I'm you know, I'm I'm really looking for people who use basketball to help people, uh not necessarily on the court, but off the court.

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Ice Cube on meeting Dr. Dre and starting his music career
quotes.excerpt: I would go hang with him and his cousin, his Dr. Dre. It's like fate.
quotes.quote: My friend down the street did all the music and all the hip hop. I would go hang with him and his cousin, his Dr. Dre. It's like fate. His cousin is Dr. Dre, his name is Sir Jinx, who was one of my earlier producers. Me and Dre got into the music industry through rap. We were always visual with our music. We were like, nobody knows what Compton, South Central, Watts, Inglewood, Long Beach, Carson are like. We got to be visual. It got to feel like a movie. It can't just be records. We were always having sound effects and always having skits to try to make these songs more real.

quotes.speaker: Ice Cube
quotes.summary_phrase: Transitioning from audio storytelling to the film Boyz n the Hood
quotes.excerpt: It was just about like, okay, the stuff we did on audio, now we get to do a visual version.
quotes.quote: One of my songs, Boyz n the Hood, a song I wrote for Easy E, turns on John Singleton. John Singleton is the director of Boyz n the Hood, the movie, and he basically discovers me and pursues me for a couple of years to actually do the movie. Once I did it, it was just about like, okay, the stuff we did on audio, now we get to do a visual version of it and show the world how we grew up and what obstacles we had to deal with. It feels seamless because I wrote the song Boyz n the Hood and I did Boyz n the Hood the movie.
